prs.title: fix(router): the success-rate sample floor counts observations, not selections
prs.body:
Closes #559.

## Problem

`min_ble_samples_before_success_rate_escalation` (default 5) is documented as the number of delivery samples needed before the low-success-rate rule applies. `update_history` pushed one success-ratio sample on every `select_transport` call from the cumulative counts, whether or not anything new had been observed. One failure on a fresh link became five identical 0.0 samples after five sends, which met the floor with no new evidence. `is_emergency_switch_needed` and `should_escalate_to_wifi` both read that window. #557 was the BLE case of this.

## Change

- `TransportHistory` remembers the `(success_count, failure_count)` of its last sample and takes a new one only when those change (`observe_outcome_counts`). The sample value is still the cumulative ratio.
- When a source halves its counts to stay bounded (the engine's `ObservedStats::compact` does), the counts have moved, so that is one sample. Reading the halved counts again is not.
- `test_low_success_rate_escalation_gated_by_sample_floor` pinned the old reading. It now asserts that five selections over unchanged counts do **not** trip the rule, and that five count changes do.
- New `test_success_ratio_sample_taken_once_per_count_change` covers the zero, repeat and halving cases.
- `docs/dors.md` config table and a CHANGELOG `Fixed` entry.

## Verification

- Negative control: with the change check removed, the rewritten test fails at the "unchanged counts must not advance the floor" assertion.
- `cargo test -p offline-protocol-router --lib`: 69 passed.
- `cargo test -p offline-protocol --lib`: 2058 passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.

Independent of #558: this branch is cut from `main`, and the two touch different files apart from CHANGELOG.

prs.title: fix: one lost inbound BLE fragment no longer marks BLE as a failing link
prs.body:
## Summary

One lost inbound Bluetooth fragment marked BLE as a failing link for the life of the process.

- **The cause.** When a partial message idled out of the reassembly cache or was evicted at capacity, `BleTransport` counted it as a failed send. Nothing ever counted a successful one: `record_send_success` never had a production caller, `ble_return_fragment` is a no-op, and no bridge reports a write outcome. So BLE's own counters could only read `0 / N`.
- **Why it spread.** The transport manager merged the engine's acknowledgement-based observations only into a transport reporting no counts of its own. After the first drop, every later acknowledgement for BLE was discarded. The comment above that check predicted this failure.
- **The effect.** DORS samples the ratio once per selection, so within five sends the window average was 0.0. That trips the low-success-rate escalation and, where Wi-Fi Direct is available, the emergency switch that bypasses hysteresis, cooldown and the stability window. `get_transport_metrics` reported a 0% delivery ratio and a 100% error rate to the app.

## What changes

- A reassembly drop is no longer a delivery sample. `BleTransport` never writes its own success or failure counts, and the two orphan methods are removed.
- The manager's merge is explicit by transport type. Internet, Reticulum and Nostr have a send confirmation loop and keep their own counts. BLE and Wi-Fi Direct always take the engine's. The match is exhaustive, so a new transport has to choose.
- The `ble_return_fragment` comment no longer claims the transport layer confirms sends.
- The transport state machine doc gains the invariant, and the CHANGELOG has Fixed and Removed entries.

## Tests

Five new tests. Four fail on main and pass here, checked in a separate worktree. The fifth guards the other side of the merge rule and passes on both.

| Test | On main |
|------|---------|
| `a_capacity_eviction_is_not_a_send_failure` | fails |
| `an_idle_expired_assembly_is_not_a_send_failure` (no expiry test existed) | fails |
| `engine_observations_win_over_a_mesh_transports_own_counts` | fails |
| `a_dropped_inbound_fragment_does_not_escalate_ble`: a real BLE transport, a capacity eviction through `on_fragment_received_from`, then eight sends | fails at the escalation assertion |
| `a_confirmation_loop_transport_keeps_its_own_counts` | passes |

Not run on hardware. The end-to-end test is the reproduction.

## Not in this PR

DORS's sample floor counts selections, not observations (`dors.rs:1259`), so it cannot gate a stale ratio on any transport. It needs its own change and a rewrite of the test that pins the current reading. Filed as #559.

## Related issues

Closes #557

## Type of change

- [x] `fix` — bug fix
- [x] `docs` — documentation only

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` passes
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --lib` passes (13 binaries, 0 failures); `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` passes
- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits; the transport commit is marked `!` for the two removed public methods
- [x] Docs / `CHANGELOG.md` updated
- [x] No new `unsafe`
- [x] UDL unchanged, so no binding regeneration
